fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the street-facing driveway entrance to help responders confirm the correct property at night or in low visibility.
• Mark any gate latches or access points along the perimeter fencing with reflective tape or paint so responders can locate them quickly.
• Trim vegetation along the access drive to maintain clearance for emergency vehicles on both sides and overhead.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the utility area so responders can reach utility shutoffs without obstruction.
• Keep any gates controlling side access unlocked or secured with a knox-type lock to allow responders through without delay.
• Post a visible property diagram or address placard near the primary entry point showing the location of the detached structure, utility area, and equipment storage area.
• Clear a walking path along the side of the main residence wide enough for a responder carrying equipment to move between the front and rear of the property.
• Keep the area around the equipment storage area clear of parked vehicles and loose materials so responders can approach from multiple directions.
• Confirm that the vehicle parking area does not block the access drive during an emergency by marking or posting no-parking boundaries near the drive entrance.
• Keep the detached structure clearly labeled or numbered if it is not visible from the street, so responding crews do not have to search the property to locate it.

wildfire.recommendations:
Based on the observations provided (tree cluster and scattered trees visible on the property), here are the mitigation recommendations:

• Thin trees within the cluster to create space between the canopies and reduce the ability of fire to move from tree to tree.
• Remove dead branches from trees in the cluster, starting from the ground up.
• Trim lower branches on scattered trees to raise the canopy height above ground level.
• Clear any dead leaves, needles, or small branches that have fallen and accumulated beneath the tree cluster.
• Thin smaller trees at the edges of the cluster to increase separation between the cluster and any nearby structures.
• Remove any shrubs or small plants growing directly beneath trees in the cluster that could carry fire upward into the tree canopies.
• Keep the area beneath scattered trees free of accumulated dead plant material on the ground.
